item_taken.first_six_words: Empty cell: an order by one
item_taken.why: The case is an order by one monotone property (spring to tide, nine reaches) folded into rows by a second property (riffle, pool, backwater) leaving one address with full cells on three sides whose occupants fixed the description of what must sit there (bottom-living, still water, salt-tolerant: flounder or goby) five months before it was seen, and the tell is met on the Empty cell side since the cell had neighbours on three sides, not fewer than two; not Endpoint demand (7), although the plan's last line conscripted the tide end, because that item yields a member with no case, the axis's word with most in front of it, whereas the flounder was fixed by three full neighbours and the pool column and was then caught; not Quadrat (14), where a square fixes nothing about its occupant and can only be visited, since here the neighbours fixed the description; not Diagonal (17), since the six marine species of 2024 were netted below the weir, outside the grid, not constructed from the list against itself, and the case itself marks that closing as the sending map's stall travelling with it.

reasoning: The rule partitions the case's contents, not the case as a whole: the address and description that full neighbours fix for an empty cell stay on form-yields, and the pleasure of pointing at what ought to be there before finding it goes to discovery-delights. The case holds both halves as dated facts. The mechanism is the grid, the empty ninth-reach pool, and its three full neighbours plus the pool column. The pointing before finding is Rask's line of 11 January 2021, 'Reach 9 pool. Something lives here ... a flounder, or a goby. Look at low water in June', and the finding is the three juvenile flounder of 14 June 2021 with her evening line 'The sea comes up the Vael', which is the recognition the rule names. Since the case contains a discoverer pointing before finding, the rule places it on the target's side, and Empty cell's own text says it adds to discovery-delights' pleasure of pointing at what ought to be there. What changes across is the foreground: at the target the case is an encounter between a discoverer and a thing discovered, and the grid becomes what she was holding when she pointed, not the item. The closing of the report at the weir, the claim of completeness, and the six marine species netted in 2024 below the weir do not fall under this rule; the case declares them as its own, so they travel intact and unreframed, since no pointing preceded them and the second team found by sampling, not by pointing.
case_out: An encounter between a discoverer and the thing discovered: Hanne Rask, a freshwater ecologist surveying the fishes of the river Vael from 2019 to 2021, had laid the survey in March 2019 on one named axis, 'from the spring to the tide', nine reaches from the spring at Kell to the tidal weir at Orm, folded into three rows by habitat, riffle, pool, and backwater, twenty-seven cells each to be netted, with the plan's last line ordering the salt-tolerant end of every row at reach nine. By the close of the 2020 season twenty-six cells held at least one species and one was empty, the pool of the ninth reach, the last above the weir, with full neighbours on three sides: the ninth reach's riffle holding the three-spined stickleback, the ninth reach's backwater holding the eel, and the pool column running reach by reach from trout through grayling and chub to the bream and roach of the eighth reach, stiller and warmer at every step. What changed between her and the pool before anything was found: on 11 January 2021 she pointed at the empty cell and described its occupant from its neighbours, writing 'Reach 9 pool. Something lives here. Bottom-living, still water, takes the salt that comes up on spring tides: a flounder, or a goby. Look at low water in June.' What changed when it was found: on 14 June 2021, seining the ninth-reach pool at low water, she took three juvenile flounder, a marine flatfish that ascends rivers, and wrote that evening, 'The sea comes up the Vael.' The pointing preceded the catch by five months; the description was drawn from the three full neighbours and the pool column, and the fish that arrived was the salt-tolerant end the plan's last line had ordered for every row. The mechanism that made the pointing precise, the address and description the full neighbours fixed, stays on form-yields and is not the item here. The following facts travel with the case as its own and are not part of the encounter: her final report of October 2021 lists thirty species, the flounder last admitted and the only marine one, gives every one of the twenty-seven cells an occupant, and closes, the fauna of the Vael, spring to tide, is complete; below the weir the river runs two further kilometres to the sea, which the report does not sample; in 2024 a second team netting the weir pool and the reach below it took mullet, bass, smelt, sand goby, sprat, and sand smelt, six marine species, none in her list, found by netting and not preceded by any pointing; the same axis whose tide end yielded the flounder closed the walk at the weir, and that closing is the stall the sending map keeps.
